{{Short description|American chemist}}
[[File:KSC-20180131-PH KLS01 0162 (40011238771).jpg|thumb|]]
'''John Long Meisenheimer Sr.''' (June 21, 1933 – January 7, 2023) was an American [[chemist]] who was a Professor Emeritus of Chemistry (1963–1999) and EKU Foundation Professor (1994–1996) at [[Eastern Kentucky University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.foundationprofessors.eku.edu/past-recipients-year|title=Past Recipients by Year &#124; Society of Foundation Professors &#124; Eastern Kentucky University}}</ref> 

On October 31, 1957, he was the Launch and Flight Weather Officer for the first U.S., intercontinental missile (Snark). In 1958, as the Launch Weather Officer for [[Explorer 1]], the first U.S. [[satellite]], he delayed America's entry into the [[Space Race]] for two days with his correct forecasts of extreme upper air [[wind shear]].<ref>History of Rocketry and Astronautics,, Ed. Kristen Lattu, pgs 255-256</ref> On the third day, January 31, his forecast was for the jet stream to move far enough away from [[Cape Canaveral]] for the upper air winds to allow an evening launch. Dr. [[Kurt Debus]], the launch director, accepted this forecast and ordered the missile to be fueled. At about 10:48 pm, Explorer 1 was successfully launched. 

From 1964 to 1970 he was a member of the Commonwealth of Kentucky's Longrifle Team that competed against teams from other states. Because of his participation in this competition he was commissioned an Honorary [[Kentucky Colonel]] in 1967 by Governor Edward Breathitt. In 1969 he won the Indiana Open Flintlock Championship competing against marksmen from six states. In 1992 he saved lives by discovering radioactive [[depleted uranium]] was used in the manufacture of  [[frizzen]]s used in [[muzzle-loading flintlock rifles]].<ref>Meisenheimer and C. Laird. A Hazardous Frizzen-Facing Material. Muzzle Blasts; August 1992: 36-37.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=20 January 2009 |title=Depleted Uranium Frizzen (1970s, 1980s) |url=https://www.orau.org/ptp/collection/consumer%20products/dufrizzen.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210330145858/https://www.orau.org/ptp/collection/consumer%20products/dufrizzen.htm |archive-date=30 March 2021 |website=Oak Ridge Associated Universities}}</ref> 

He plays a recurring role of Pappy 5X in the book and [[webisode]] series the Zombie Cause. His biography is in the 2021 edition of Who'sWho In America,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.zombiecause.com/Cast.html |title=The Zombie Cause Cast Doc Lucky Meisenheimer |website=www.zombiecause.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130114035536/http://www.zombiecause.com/Cast.html |archive-date=2013-01-14}}</ref>

Meisenheimer died from [[transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy]] on January 7, 2023, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. John Long Meisenheimer Sr. |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/john-meisenheimer-obituary?id=52551433 |website=Legacy |access-date=22 December 2024}}</ref>
